info.name: Ecommerce Platform API
info.description:
Complete API collection for the Spring Boot microservices ecommerce platform.

Services covered: auth, product, inventory, order, payment, notification.
All requests go through the API Gateway at `{{base_url}}` (default http://localhost:8080).

Quick start:
1. Run `make up` from the repo root.
2. Open the **Setup → Bootstrap admin login** request and run it (uses ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_PASSWORD from .env).
3. Run **Auth → Register customer**, then **Auth → Login (customer)** — it auto-saves `access_token`.
4. Use any of the customer-scoped requests (catalog, cart, checkout, orders).
5. To exercise seller flows, run **Admin → Promote user to seller** with the customer's userId, then re-login.

Tokens are cached in collection variables (`access_token`, `admin_token`). Tests at the request level capture order ids, product ids, etc. for chaining.

item.name: Setup
item.description: One-shot helpers for bootstrapping a new local environment.

request.description: Logs in the bootstrap admin (created on first start when ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_PASSWORD env vars are set in .env). Saves the JWT to `admin_token` so admin requests in the rest of the collection can use it.
Used by every backend service to verify JWTs. Two keys here means a key rotation is in flight.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Public auth endpoints + signed-in user self-service. JWT is RS256 signed; access tokens are 15 min, refresh tokens 30 days delivered as an HttpOnly cookie.

request.description: Public registration. Always assigns ROLE_CUSTOMER. The previous self-elevation to SELLER is intentionally removed; an admin must promote sellers via /api/admin/users/{id}/roles.
OAuth2-style password grant. Returns access token in body. Refresh token is delivered as an HttpOnly Secure SameSite=Strict cookie.

Reuses the refresh-token cookie from the previous login. Postman must keep cookies enabled. Family-based reuse detection: if a previously-rotated refresh token is presented, the entire family is revoked.
Blacklists the access token in Redis (TTL = remaining lifetime) and revokes the refresh token.
Authenticated-only (the previous permitAll bug is fixed). Uses the JWT subject as the user id.
Open in a browser — completes via OAuth2 success handler which sets the refresh-token cookie and 302s to the frontend with the access token in the URL fragment.

item.name: Admin
item.description: All endpoints require fine-grained authorities (admin:users:read|write, admin:roles:read|write).

request.description: Replaces the user's role set. After this call the user must re-login to get a fresh JWT carrying the new authorities.

exec: if (pm.response.code === 409) { console.warn('Category exists; using stable cat-apparel id'); pm.collectionVariables.set('category_id', 'cat-apparel'); return; }

item.name: Products
item.description: Catalog. Reads are public. Writes require the seller's JWT (or an admin's). Image URLs are intentionally null until the image pipeline ships.

item.name: Inventory
item.description: Atomic reservation backed by Mongo `findAndModify` with `$expr` so concurrent requests cannot over-commit.

request.description: Idempotency at the saga level is provided by the calling order-service. Reserves 1 unit; fails with 409 INSUFFICIENT_STOCK if the atomic guard rejects it.

Orders
item.description: Order saga. Creating an order: snapshots product price via ProductClient, reserves stock per item via InventoryClient (rollback-on-failure), persists, and emits OrderEvent.CREATED so payment-service can initiate the PaymentIntent.

request.description: Customers see their own orders; admins see all orders.
Customer can cancel their own non-shipped order. Triggers stock release via InventoryClient.

item.name: Payments
item.description: Payment-service. Stripe (when STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is set) or SandboxGateway. Webhook signing uses HMAC-SHA256 with the format `t=<unix>,v1=<hex>`.

request.description: Manual confirm — useful in dev with the SandboxGateway. With Stripe, the gateway drives status via webhook instead.
Set `amount` to a value < total for partial refund (status becomes PARTIALLY_REFUNDED). Null = full refund.

Pre-request script computes the HMAC over the JSON body and stores it in the {{webhook_signature}} variable. Format: `t=<unix>,v1=<hex>`. Replace `webhook_secret` collection var with PAYMENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET from your .env.

item.name: Notifications
item.description: Mongo-persisted notifications. Idempotent on `sourceEventId` so the same Kafka event never produces two emails. MailHog UI: http://localhost:8025

item.name: End-to-end happy path
item.description:
A scripted run-through of the full saga. Use Postman's Collection Runner on this folder.

1. Bootstrap admin login → admin_token.
2. Register customer → user_id.
3. Login (customer) → access_token.
4. Create category (admin) → category_id.
5. (You'll need an existing seller; promote the customer or use a fixture.)
6. Create product (seller) → product_id.
7. Create inventory item.
8. Create order → order_id, order_number.
9. Create payment → payment_id, payment_reference.
10. Webhook (HMAC) → marks payment COMPLETED.
11. Get order — should be CONFIRMED with paymentStatus=COMPLETED.
12. List my notifications — should contain the order-confirmation email.

// in the runner this is OK since each request runs sequentially and Kafka is fast.
